1.note: Isaiah says **seven women will seize one man** as an extreme statement for emphasis. He means that so many men will have died that very few will remain. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [so few men will remain that many women will beg to share even one man]
Yahweh is using the phrase **in that day** to refer to a specific time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [at that time]

The expression **let your name be called over us** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [please marry us and give us your name]

The women are using **let your name be called over us** as a common expression of the culture to mean “let us be known as belonging to you through marriage.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [let us be known as your wives]

This is an imperative, but it communicates a polite request rather than a command. If the imperative does not communicate a polite request for your readers, then use a form in your language that communicates a polite request. It may be helpful to add an expression such as “please” to make this clear. Alternate translation: [Please take away our reproach]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **reproach**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [our shameful feeling that comes from having no husband]

2.note: Isaiah is speaking as if what **Yahweh** causes to grow were a** branch**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [what Yahweh causes to grow]
To translate the phrase **In that day**, see how you translated it in [4:1](ta:04).
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **splendor** and **glory**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [beautiful and glorifying]

The terms **splendor** and **glory** mean similar things. Isaiah is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [for great splendor] or [for glorious splendor]

Isaiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and the fruit of the land will be for pride and for adornment]

Isaiah is speaking as if all the produce of the **land** were **fruit**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the crops that the land produces]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **pride** and **adornment**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [for things to be proud of and for beautiful adornment]

The phrase **pride and adornment** expresses a single idea. The word adornment tells more about pride. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [for pride-inspiring adornment]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **escape**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for those who survived in Israel]

3.q: וְ⁠הָיָ֣ה הַ⁠נִּשְׁאָ֣ר בְּ⁠צִיּ֗וֹן וְ⁠הַ⁠נּוֹתָר֙ בִּ⁠יר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם קָד֖וֹשׁ יֵאָ֣מֶר ל֑⁠וֹ כָּל־הַ⁠כָּת֥וּב לַ⁠חַיִּ֖ים בִּ⁠ירוּשָׁלִָֽם
3.note: These two phrases **the one remained in Zion and the one left in Jerusalem** and **everyone written for life in Jerusalem** mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [And it will be, everyone written for life in Jerusalem and remaining in Zion will be called “Holy,”]
Isaiah is using the word translated as **And it will be** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

The expression **the one left in Jerusalem** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and the one whom God left in Jerusalem]
The pronoun **him** refers to each person who has remained in Zion and been left in Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [each one of them]

Isaiah is speaking as if God’s decision about who would be **written for life in Jerusalem** were something written in a book. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [everyone whose name God has recorded in his book so that they will live in Jerusalem]

The expression **everyone written for life in Jerusalem** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [everyone whom Yahweh has written down for life in Jerusalem]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **life**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to live]

3.q: הַ⁠נִּשְׁאָ֣ר בְּ⁠צִיּ֗וֹן וְ⁠הַ⁠נּוֹתָר֙ בִּ⁠יר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם קָד֖וֹשׁ יֵאָ֣מֶר ל֑⁠וֹ
3.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about what will be said of the person before the information about who the person is. Alternate translation: [“Holy” will be said of the one who remained in Zion and the one left in Jerusalem, that is, of everyone written for life in Jerusalem]

The expression **“Holy” will be said of him** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people will call him “Holy”]

4.q: אִ֣ם ׀ רָחַ֣ץ אֲדֹנָ֗⁠י אֵ֚ת צֹאַ֣ת בְּנוֹת־צִיּ֔וֹן וְ⁠אֶת־דְּמֵ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם יָדִ֣יחַ מִ⁠קִּרְבָּ֑⁠הּ בְּ⁠ר֥וּחַ מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּ⁠בְ⁠ר֥וּחַ בָּעֵֽר
4.note: Isaiah is using **when the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and has cleansed the blood of Jerusalem from its midst by a spirit of judgment and by a spirit of burning** to describe something that was ongoing. This provides the background for the events described in the previous verse. Connect this clause to the story in a way that makes it clear in your language that this clause is describing something that was ongoing in the background. Alternate translation: [while the Lord was washing away the filth of the daughters of Zion and was cleansing the blood of Jerusalem from its midst by a spirit of judgment and by a spirit of burning.]

Isaiah is speaking as if the moral impurity of the people were **filth** that could be **washed away**. Your language may have a comparable expression, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [removed the moral impurity of the daughters of Zion]

Isaiah is speaking as if the guilt of violence in Jerusalem were **blood** that could be **cleansed** from the city. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [has cleansed Jerusalem of its violence]

Here, **the blood** represents “the violence and bloodshed.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the bloodguilt of Jerusalem]

The phrase **a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning** expresses a single idea. The word burning tells more about judgment. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [by a judging spirit that burns away what is wrong]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **judgment** and **burning**, you could express the same ideas in other ways. Alternate translation: [judging]

5.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **glory**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [that glorious site]

5.q: וּ⁠בָרָ֣א יְהוָ֡ה עַל֩ כָּל־מְכ֨וֹן הַר־צִיּ֜וֹן וְ⁠עַל־מִקְרָאֶ֗⁠הָ עָנָ֤ן יוֹמָם֙ וְ⁠עָשָׁ֔ן וְ⁠נֹ֛גַהּ אֵ֥שׁ לֶהָבָ֖ה לָ֑יְלָה כִּ֥י & כָּל־כָּב֖וֹד חֻפָּֽה
5.note: Here, **for** marks **over all of the glory will be a canopy** as the purpose of Yahweh creating the **cloud**, **smoke**, and **fire** over **Mount Zion**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh will create over all of the site of Mount Zion and over its assemblies a cloud and smoke by day and the shining of a fire, a flame, by night, in order that there will be a canopy over all of the glory]

Isaiah is speaking as if God’s protection over his people were a **canopy**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [over all of the glory there will be a protective covering]

Isaiah is referring to all time by naming two major components, **day** and **night**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [for over all of the glory {will be} a canopy at all times]

6.note: A **booth** is a kind of temporary shelter made from branches and other materials. If your readers would not be familiar with what a booth is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a simple shelter]

Isaiah is speaking as if God’s protection were a physical **refuge** and **shelter**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and for protection and for safety]
